title: Color the Triangle Red
exampleStatus: Source examples not copied; worked illustrations are independently authored in clarification.
summary: The triangular board contains n*n initially white unit triangles. Neighbors share an edge. Choose initial red cells; repeatedly turn a white cell red when it has at least two red neighbors. Return coordinates of a MINIMUM-CARDINALITY initial set that eventually colors the whole board. Any optimal set is accepted.
clarification: Authored worked example n=4: seed (1,1),(2,3),(3,2),(4,1),(4,3),(4,5),(4,7). Then color (2,2),(2,1),(4,2),(3,1),(4,4),(3,3),(3,4),(4,6),(3,5). Each step has two red neighbors. Optimality: the board has 16 cells and 18 adjacency edges. Each nonseed needs two edges to earlier red cells; each edge can count at most once. Thus 2*(16-k)<=18, so k>=7, achieved here.
constraintsReportedBySource: 1<=n<=1000; row r has 2*r-1 unit triangles; coordinates are one-based.
